    {
      "name": "kernel",
      "member": true,
      "evidence": "Kernel-scoped refactor and implementation under src/kernel/ designed to allow libbitcoinkernel consumers to read block storage concurrently.",
      "band": "P2",
      "score": 0.68,
      "reason_tag": "new feature",
      "rationale": "Enables external applications building on libbitcoinkernel (such as Electrs or Esplora) to inspect block and header metadata concurrently without shutting down Bitcoin Core. Removing the LevelDB dependency for block and header storage is strategically important for kernel library usability."
    },
    {
      "name": "mempool",

      "rationale": "Does not touch mempool data structures, acceptance, or transaction policy."
    },

      "name": "tests",

      "evidence": "Touches benchmarks and fuzz tests specifically to test the new block tree storage implementation.",
      "band": "Unranked",

      "rationale": "The added benchmark and unit/fuzz tests test the new block storage backend rather than test harness infrastructure."
    },

    },
    {
      "name": "validation",
      "member": true,
      "evidence": "Carries the 'UTXO Db and Indexes' label and replaces the node's mandatory CBlockTreeDB with a flat-file WAL store.",
      "band": "P2",
      "score": 0.62,
      "reason_tag": "new feature",
      "rationale": "Replacing CBlockTreeDB with a flat-file and WAL store fundamentally changes block-index persistence, migration, and crash safety. Because this substantively changes core validation storage while primarily serving kernel consumer concurrency, it spans both areas and requires dedicated validation scrutiny regarding crash recovery and atomicity invariants."
